title: Blend If in Photoshop: Sky Replacement and Color Grading (Day 17, PHLEARN)
summary: PHLEARN's Day 17 in the 30 Days of Photoshop series demonstrates the Blend If feature in Photoshop as a non-destructive method to composite images by controlling visibility with light levels. The video covers basic concepts of Blend If, how to access and interpret the two sliders (current layer and underlying layer), and the use of control points and feathering (via Alt/Option) to create realistic blends. A practical sky replacement workflow illustrates unlinking layer and layer mask, selecting the sky, and adjusting Blend If across both current and underlying layers to harmonize the new sky with the original lighting. The tutorial also explores color grading techniques using a solid color fill layer and a gradient map, showing how Blend If can modulate visibility by color channels, highlights, or shadows. Overall, the video emphasizes non-destructive, adjustable blending for realistic compositing, with before/after comparisons to verify improvements.
